This 2025 BMW M5 Failing To Sell for Over $93,000 Is Quite Interesting
16 photos
Photo: Cars & Bids
This 2025 BMW M5 only has 2,800 miles on the clock and recently failed to sell at auction where the highest anybody would bid was $93,000. The MSRP on this thing was $130,225, which goes to show just how rapidly the G90 M5 is depreciating once it leaves the showroom floor. This is great news for buyers, because they're getting a lot of car for the money.
Despite its controversial nature, the latest-generation BMW M5 is still a pretty awesome car. What's controversial about it, you ask? Come on - the weight gain, the plug-in hybrid powertrain, the polarizing design. You name it! The thing is, the plug-in hybrid system is actually one of its strong suits, and the design isn't bad at all, especially with those wider arches.
The result on this car is revealing, with the bidding maxing out at $93,000. It points to a tension between what the G90 M5 costs new and what at least some buyers are currently prepared to pay for a used one. People are extremely interested in bargain-hunting on this car, and it's easy to understand why. On paper, the new M5 is a beast, regardless of how much it weighs.
Now, if this was my car, given the mileage, I'm pretty sure I'd have held out too. It can still fetch more than $93,000. Not a lot more, but more. I absolutely love the Isle of Man Green Metallic exterior colorway. It's one of the best colors ever that you can spec on a fast Bimmer.
Other notable equipment includes the 20" and 21" Style 951M wheels, both the Carbon and Executive packages, the Driving Assistant Plus system, heated and ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, carbon fiber high gloss silver thread interior trim, a Bowers & Wilkins surround sound system, and more. I'm also a big fan of the Kyalami Orange and Black upholstery. It's the exact same spec I drove during my review of the G90 M5 back in 2025 - you can read all about it here .
Spoiler alert, great car. Absolutely tremendous feat of engineering. It's not as fun to drive as an M5 Comp but as an overall package, it just delivers on everything it promises.
Photo: Cars & Bids It all starts with the 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine, working alongside an electric motor and a 14.8-kWh lithium-ion battery. The combined system output is 717 horsepower (727 ps) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed automatic transmission.
The new M5 can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in just 3.4 seconds, before maxing out at 190 mph (305 kph) with the optional M Driver's Pack. Furthermore, you can drive this car on electric power alone at speeds of up to 87 mph (140 kph), which means that you can literally use this as an EV 100% of the time, should you choose to (in favorable conditions, of course).
